text:
sara: quick follow-up from the rollout metadata RFC — thinking about adding a tiny compatibility hint to help client resolvers prefer compatible variants. sketch below. thoughts?

sara: proposed field: `compatibility_hint` with values like `strict|minor|backward` plus `compat_hash` to cheaply detect incompatible model blobs. example: 
```
{
  "anchor": "model-A@v2.1.0",
  "compatibility_hint": "minor",
  "compat_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "rolling_window": "2026-05-01/2026-06-01"
}
```

tom: i like the small surface area. two questions: 1) where do we compute compat_hash? build-time via model-ingest pipeline? 2) what does `minor` mean programmatically to the resolver?

eli: +1 for the hint. for build-time: model-ingest should emit the hash and a compatibility-level computed by the model-onboarding job (weights + tokenizer shape). not perfect but better than nothing.

marc: worried about relying on heuristic. if clients start preferring by hint we must ensure we don't accidentally split traffic when hint is wrong. also storage: compat_hash adds index pressure. how big are we expecting these objects to be?

sara: agreed on safety. plan is to make client behavior conservative: hint is only used for tie-breaking and for fast local checks; server-side routing still enforces strict compatibility rules before handshake. so mistaken hints cause no outage, just suboptimal routing.

eli: regarding size — compat_hash is a single short string (sha256), metadata objects are tiny. indexing is fine. bigger cost is onboarding compute to compute compatibility fingerprint; that's a one-time job per model-version.

tom: implementation note: add new enum `compatibility_level` (none|backward|minor|breaking) and add `compat_fingerprint` string. default to `none`. update rollout service to honor levels during `canary` and `fallback` decisions.

marc: ops question — how will this interact with pin eviction? if a pinned pool has mixed `minor` vs `breaking` variants, do we prefer minor for affinity? should pin affinity scoreboard include hint weight?

sara: good point. proposal: pin-affinity remains primarily based on explicit anchor and lease. compatibility hint only affects routing within the same affinity bucket. so pinned pool won't evict based on hint alone.

eli: testing plan: unit tests for resolver logic + simulation traffic runs with randomized wrong hints to ensure no user-visible regressions. also add evals that compare outputs across minor-labeled variants to validate the label over time.

tom: +1. also add telemetry: `rollout.hint_used` boolean and `rollout.hint_mismatch` counter to detect places where hint diverged from actual compatibility.

marc: sounds safe. please add migration steps: default existing models to `none`, backfill computed fingerprints, and roll out resolver changes behind a feature flag. ops can flip once we have telemetry.

arch-bot: ACTIONS: 1) sara to draft short schema patch text for the registry API. 2) eli to add compat fingerprint job to onboarding. 3) tom to add resolver flag + telemetry. 4) marc to validate pin-affinity no-op. ETA EOW.

sara: thanks — i'll draft the patch and link here. :thumbsup:
